title: Con miras a: el propósito detrás de una acción

sections.content: Con miras a (with a view to, aimed at) states the forward-looking purpose behind an institutional or policy decision -- common in formal writing about reforms, laws, and constitutions. It's followed by an infinitive or a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Brasil promulgó una nueva constitución, redactada con miras a garantizar amplios derechos sociales.
items.english: Brazil enacted a new constitution, drafted with a view to guaranteeing broad social rights.

items.spanish: Colombia convocó una asamblea constituyente con miras a modernizar un sistema político centenario.
items.english: Colombia convened a constituent assembly with a view to modernizing a century-old political system.

items.spanish: Paraguay aprobó una nueva constitución diseñada con miras a impedir cualquier concentración excesiva de poder.
items.english: Paraguay passed a new constitution designed with a view to preventing any excessive concentration of power.

items.spanish: La región creó tribunales electorales independientes con miras a garantizar elecciones limpias.
items.english: The region created independent electoral tribunals with a view to guaranteeing clean elections.

sections.content: Con miras a is more formal and forward-looking than para -- it fits especially well when describing the long-term institutional goal behind a specific reform or document, rather than an immediate practical purpose.
